pairs.description: Ginkgo biloba combined with warfarin increases bleeding risk and potential spontaneous hemorrhagic events including intracranial hemorrhage.
pairs.mechanism: Ginkgolide B serves as a potent antagonist of platelet-activating factor (PAF), compounding warfarin's anticoagulant mechanism.

pairs.description: Co-administration of ginkgo and aspirin results in dual antiplatelet inhibition, causing documented clinical bleeding episodes such as spontaneous hyphema.
pairs.mechanism: Additive platelet antiaggregatory activity combining cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition by aspirin with PAF antagonism by ginkgolides.

pairs.description: Combining ginkgo with NSAIDs like ibuprofen increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and prolonged bleeding times.
pairs.mechanism: Additive impairment of primary platelet plug formation and gastric mucosal cytoprotective prostaglandin suppression.

pairs.description: Ginkgo biloba extracts may significantly lower plasma concentrations of efavirenz, jeopardizing suppression of human immunodeficiency virus.
pairs.mechanism: Induction of cytochrome P450 2B6 by terpenoid constituents of ginkgo extract.
